summary: Stop owned resource executions when mission steps are cancelled or fail

schema.detail: No client schema, code generation or persisted format changes.

rules.detail: The execution host matches native run, step and attempt ownership during shell reconciliation. Failed, cancelled and superseded attempts request cancellation through generation-fenced process-group SIGTERM, with non-waiting SIGKILL signalling after the existing five-second grace period. Exit observation and custody retirement remain separate. Finally steps remain eligible until their own attempt ends.

compatibility.detail: Mission cleanup includes owned shell executions and waits for exit, retirement and receipt publication until the cleanup deadline. At expiry it records an explicit execution custody unconfirmed outcome and terminalizes the run without terminalizing the execution or releasing membership custody. Later shell sweeps continue retirement. Step-declared drivers retain the existing exact-stop, terminate-request and kill-deadline path.

downtime.detail: No migration; behavior changes when the reconciler is restarted.

recovery.detail: Active shell reconciliation also cancels executions whose owning attempt has already ended, including after restart. Existing cancellation offsets and terminal receipts remain authoritative.
